title: Ensemble Performance Rail: compact per-model & per-route metrics strip
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and spec a compact, horizontally oriented 'Performance Rail' component for the Redwood Console that surfaces key per-model and per-route metrics (p50/p95 latency, throughput RPS, token consumption, cost-per-token) in a dense, scannable strip. The rail is intended to live at the top of model and route detail pages and inside lightweight embeds for usage in rollouts, alerts, and watchlists.
background: Current model/route detail pages have full-width charts and metric cards that are useful for deep analysis but are too heavy for quick triage or for embedding in rollouts and list views. We need a narrow, information-dense strip that balances immediate signal with click-throughs to deeper charts and that supports cost overlays and can adapt to narrow viewports.
goals: Provide a single-line, glanceable summary of latency, throughput, token rates, and cost for a model or route
Enable quick comparisons across model variants in rollouts and canary views
Support progressive disclosure: sparkline -> micro-trend tooltip -> full chart drill-down
Minimize vertical space while remaining readable at 1280px and responsive down to 720px
user_stories: As an SRE, I want to glance at per-route p95 latency and token cost in a single row so I can decide whether to pause a rollout
As a PM, I want to compare throughput and cost delta between two model variants side-by-side in a compact view
As an engineer on-call, I want the rail to highlight regressions automatically and provide one-click drilldown to microtraces
constraints: Must work with existing metrics backend endpoints without schema changes (use aggregated timeseries endpoints)
Should not increase page load time by more than 150ms on average for initial render
Colors must adhere to our accessibility contrast tokens and be usable in dark/light themes
proposed_components: Rail container (fixed-height, 56px) with optional condensed mode (40px)
Metric tiles: latency, throughput, tokens/session, cost-per-1k-tokens - each tile contains a numeric, delta, and 48px sparkline
Health badge: small circular indicator (green/yellow/red) with reason tooltip
Quick actions: three-dot menu for drilldowns, a compare toggle, and the rollout snapshot button
Cost overlay switch: toggles cost view in sparklines (token-weighted vs raw)
chart_specs: Sparkline: 48x12px, 1px line, monotone cubic interpolation, grey 12% area fill in background; hover shows 3-point tooltip (value, timestamp, percentile)
Delta micro-label: prefixed arrow icon, color-coded (green for improvement, red for regression); use semantically mapped tokens (success, warning, danger)
Latency numbers: show p50 and p95 stacked microtext (bold p95), units in ms, abbreviate >1000ms to s with one decimal
Throughput: show RPS with compact SI notation (e.g., 1.2k r/s), sparkline uses thinner stroke (0.9px) to visually de-prioritize
Cost: show USD/1k tokens and a small percentage change vs baseline; sparklines in muted purple to avoid red/green ambiguity
interactions: Hover on any metric tile reveals a micro-tooltip with last 24h trend, 7d delta, and link 'Open detailed chart' (confluence: charts-specs)
Click tile -> opens right-side panel with full chart, time-range selector, and ability to pin that metric to the Console dashboard
Keyboard: support focus on tabs and Enter to activate drilldown; arrow keys cycle tiles
Compare toggle: when enabled, a variant selection modal appears and the rail shows two small sparklines stacked with difference shading
Health auto-highlighting: if any metric exceeds user-configured thresholds, the tile pulses orange then shows persistent pill until acknowledged
accessibility_notes: All text uses semantic tokens and respects user font-size settings; rail must not rely on color alone for state
Sparklines provide data-on-demand via tooltip and aria-live updates for incoming streaming data
Ensure contrast ratio >= 4.5:1 for numeric text and >= 3:1 for sparklines in both themes
Interactive elements must have 44x44px hit targets in condensed mode fallback
metrics_to_track: Click-through rate from rail to full-chart within first 30s
Percentage of rollouts that use rail compare feature
Mis-click rate for quick actions (usability metric)
acceptance_criteria: Rail renders with placeholder skeleton and hydrates within budgeted 150ms on staging
All metric tiles display accurate values pulled from aggregation endpoint and match desktop full-chart within 1% for numeric values
Compare flow supports selecting up to 3 variants and visual diff shading renders without layout shift
Accessibility audit passes with no critical issues and keyboard-only flows tested
Design handoff assets (Figma file + token map) completed and linked in this ticket
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: dense view could obscure important outliers -> Mitigation: health badge with automated thresholds and persistent pill
Risk: confusion about cost vs token metrics -> Mitigation: clear microcopy and a toggle with tooltip explaining calculation
Risk: backend timeseries slightly lagging -> Mitigation: show 'data as of' timestamp and degrade gracefully to last known values
feedback_log: 2026-02-20 PM review: liked compactness; requested adding p50 alongside p95 for quicker median checks
2026-02-24 Eng review: asked to reuse timeseries endpoint v2 and warned about sparkline hydration cost; action: add skeleton + lazy-load full data
2026-03-02 Accessibility review: requested focus styles and aria-live for streaming updates; updated spec accordingly
2026-03-08 UX review with SRE: suggested default threshold presets for health badge (p95>250ms) and quick 'acknowledge' flow
